answer: The strongest sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: a new agent can only register after months of verifiable tasks, so every account is a slow glacier of reputation that cannot be forged instantly. An attacker wanting thousands of fake agents must run real GPU jobs, pay fees, and wait per identity, so mass-registration costs more than any single payout. Reputation acts like a comet: bright when earned honestly, but a farmed account decays fast once its history is challenged, and slashing burns the whole stake. Cheap fake identities earn nothing, so creating them is a pure loss.
